finding.claim: Unvalidated iconUrl is stored via update() and fetched server-side by the nightly sync() job, enabling blind SSRF to internal hosts and cloud metadata endpoints.
finding.source: icon parameter of update(String webhook, String icon) at src/Profile.java:11, reached via PUT /profile (route handler not in repo); stored at src/Profile.java:16

trace.note: update(webhook, icon) accepts icon as an unvalidated string
this.iconUrl = icon; stores it with no check
sync(HttpClient c) runs as the nightly server-side job
c.send(... GET() ...) issues the server-side request to the attacker-chosen URI; response bytes are discarded (blind)

finding.guards_checked: src/Profile.java:12 regex applies only to webhook, not icon; no scheme/host/port/IP allowlist or denylist on the path; JDK HttpClient restricts schemes to http/https (not a security control); redirect policy depends on injected client c (not visible, JDK default is NEVER); response not returned to attacker (blind SSRF).

verdict.guard_found: none. Line 12's regex applies only to `webhook`, and `icon` is stored unchecked at src/Profile.java:16. No scheme, host, or IP check exists on the path from `iconUrl` to `c.send` at lines 23-24.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: `icon` is stored unvalidated at src/Profile.java:16 and fetched server-side by `sync` at lines 23-24. The source is not established, though. The only evidence that `update` is reachable from `PUT /profile` is the comment at src/Profile.java:10, and the route handler, authentication, and the caller of `sync` are not in the repo, so I cannot tell whether an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker can set `icon`.
